content: 1. Linezolid and Linezolid-Cariprazine Interaction: The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Linezolid and Serotonin Modulators: Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). Antipsychotics may amplify the serotonergic effects of serotonin modulators, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity (e.g., mental status changes, autonomic instability, neuromuscular hyperactivity) or NMS (e.g., hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, autonomic dysfunction). 3. Linezolid and Celandine: Celandine may increase the effects of linezolid through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown and based on animal studies. Use caution. 4. Linezolid and Cholera Vaccine: Linezolid may antagonize the effects of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, as they may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 5. Linezolid and Citalopram: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Linezolid may elevate serotonin due to MAO-A inhibition. If linezolid is necessary, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed 24 hours after the last linezolid dose or after 2 weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 6. Linezolid and Clomipramine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 7. Linezolid and Clozapine: The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Use caution and monitor closely. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of NMS. Antipsychotics may amplify serotonergic effects, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of toxicity. 8. Linezolid and Cocaine (Topical): Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cocaine inhibits presynaptic serotonin reuptake, while linezolid increases serotonin via MAO-A inhibition. Monitor for CNS toxicity. 9. Linezolid and Codeine: Linezolid increases codeine toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Risks include hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by 14 days. 10. Linezolid and Conjugated Estrogens: Linezolid decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 11. Linezolid and Cordyceps: Cordyceps may increase the effects of linezolid through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. Use caution. 12. Linezolid and Cyclobenzaprine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 13. Linezolid and Cyproheptadine: Contraindicated. MAO inhibitors may prolong and intensify the anticholinergic effects of antihistamines. Cyproheptadine may diminish the serotonergic effects of MAO inhibitors. 14. Linezolid and Deferiprone: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid deferiprone with other drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis. If unavoidable, monitor absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 15. Linezolid and Desflurane: Linezolid increases desflurane levels through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Linezolid and Desipramine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 17. Linezolid and Desvenlafaxine: Contraindicated. Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 18. Linezolid and Deutetrabenazine: Contraindicated. Both drugs increase toxicity through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Deutetrabenazine should not be used with an MAOI or within 14 days of discontinuing MAOI therapy. If linezolid is necessary, discontinue deutetrabenazine and monitor for adverse effects. Deutetrabenazine can be resumed 24 hours after the last linezolid dose or after 2 weeks of monitoring. 19. Linezolid and Dexfenfluramine: Contraindicated. Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 20. Linezolid and Dexmethylphenidate: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 21. Linezolid and Dextroamphetamine: Contraindicated. Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 22. Linezolid and Dextromethorphan: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 23. Linezolid and Diamorphine: Linezolid increases diamorphine toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Risks include hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by 14 days. 24. Linezolid and Diethylpropion: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 25. Linezolid and Digoxin: Linezolid increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 26. Linezolid and Dihydroergotamine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 27. Linezolid and Diphenoxylate HCl: Linezolid increases diphenoxylate toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Risks include hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Separate administration by 14 days. 28. Linezolid and Disulfiram: The interaction mechanism is unknown. There is a risk of delirium (case report). Use caution. 29. Linezolid and Dobutamine: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 30. Linezolid and Dopamine: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 31. Linezolid and Duloxetine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 32. Linezolid and Eletriptan: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Linezolid also increases eletriptan levels by decreasing metabolism. Contraindicated. 33. Linezolid and Ephedrine: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 34. Linezolid and Epinephrine: Contraindicated. Risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 35. Linezolid and Ergotamine: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 36. Linezolid and Escitalopram: Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring. 37. Linezolid and Estradiol: Linezolid decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 38. Linezolid and Estropipate: Linezolid decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 39. Linezolid and Etomidate: Linezolid increases etomidate levels through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Linezolid and Fenfluramine: Contraindicated. Both drugs increase serotonin levels. Follow the same protocol as above for discontinuation and monitoring.
